Scene 01

Scene 01

Fox Mulder

They said the birds refused to sing... And the thermometer fell suddenly, as if god himself had his breath stolen away. No one there dared speak aloud, as much in shame as in sorrow. They uncovered the bodies one by one. The eyes of the dead were closed, as if waiting for permission to open them. Were they still dreaming of ice cream and monkey bars, of birthday cake and no future but the afternoon? Or had their innocence been taken along with their lives, buried in the cold earth so long ago? These fates seemed too cruel, even for god to allow. Or are the tragic young born again when the world's not looking? I wanna believe so badly in a truth beyond our own, hidden and obscured from all but the most sensitive eyes.

♪♪ [ soft, ethereal ]

Fox Mulder

In the endless procession of souls, in what cannot and will not be destroyed, I want to believe we are unaware of god's eternal recompense and sadness-- that we cannot see his truth. That that which is born still lives and cannot be buried in the cold earth,

♪♪ [ continues ]

Fox Mulder

But only waits to be born again at god's behest... Where in ancient starlight we lay... In repose.

[ children chattering, laughing on TV ]

[ door opens ]

TECHNICAL SERVICE ROOM

Dana Scully

Ed truelove was 19 when he committed his first murder. He was working as a janitor at an elementary school... And they needed someone to play santa claus. He never got over the feelings it aroused. He's admitted to all of it, Mulder-- 24 separate murders. But he refuses to take blame for amber lynn lapierre. I was just handed the preliminary forensics report. Her body was not one of those found in the graves. Mulder, I know you wanted to find her out there.

Fox Mulder

He's got hours of video of her.

Dana Scully

I'm talking about your sister. I know that's who you're looking for.

Fox Mulder

Yeah. You don't know how badly I wanted her to be in one of those graves. Hard as it is to admit, I wanted to find her here riding her bike like all these other kids. I guess I just want it to be over.

Agent Mulder, Scully. There's a mr. Harold Piller here to see you.

Mr. Piller?

Agent Mulder. Agent Scully.

Yes, I hope to be.

Fox Mulder

How can we help you?

Harold Piller

I was hoping to help you.

Dana Scully

You're a police psychic.

Harold Piller

My references are on the back. I've gotten some strong hits off this case. You're looking for a little girl, but she's not among the dead. Your suspect is going to say he didn't kill her.

Fox Mulder

Did he?

Harold Piller

No. I think I can help find her.

Dana Scully

Mr. Piller, you have some interesting references here. You've worked with law enforcements in kashmir, india, myanmar, afghanistan, pakistan, khyber pass.

Harold Piller

That was a train wreck-- a horrible tragedy. They called me in to locate the bodies of seven children who were unrecovered.

Dana Scully

And did you recover them?

Harold Piller

I didn't recover them, no. But I explained what happened.

Fox Mulder

What happened?

Harold Piller

The children's bodies were transported from the accident site... By a spiritual intervention, what are known as walk-ins.

Dana Scully

Thank you, mr. Piller, but we have real work to be done.

Harold Piller

I've studied this phenomenon the world over-- at mud slides in peru, earthquakes in uzbekistan. Kids' bodies never found, never accounted for in any other way.

Fox Mulder

What happened to them?

Harold Piller

The bodies were transported from the various sites... In starlight.

Dana Scully

Please excuse us. Mulder? Mulder, please.

Fox Mulder

What is it?

Dana Scully

Mulder, you have been through so much in such a short time-- the death of your mother and the feelings it's brought up for your sister. You're vulnerable right now.

Fox Mulder

We still have a missing body-- amber lynn lapierre. She may be alive. We don't know.

Dana Scully

But this man isn't gonna help us find her, by his own admission.

Fox Mulder

It's not the first time I've heard what he's saying-- about the intervention of these walking spirits. Kathy lee tencate mentioned it to me in the prison. She said that's who took her son.

Dana Scully

Because it's foolproof, Mulder. Nobody is gonna disprove it if there's no body. And that's exactly what this man does. He gives a comforting explanation at a train wreck... Or an earthquake that everyone can live with. But the fact is the bodies are still buried.

Fox Mulder

Or maybe they are somewhere else.

Dana Scully

Like your sister? Mulder, you told me that all you wanted was for this to be over.

Fox Mulder

I do. I do.

Dana Scully

Well, then I'm going back to Washington. There's nothing more to be done here.

Scene 03

Scene 03

Fox Mulder

How long have you been doing this?

Harold Piller

A few years. I have a son who disappeared under strange circumstances. He's never been found. And then one day, I just... Started to see them.

Fox Mulder

These walk-ins, you say they-- they come and take the children. Why?

Harold Piller

In almost every case, the parents had a precognitive image... Of their child dead. Horrible visions. I believe what this is is the work of good spirits... Foretelling their fates. A fate the child was about to meet, a particularly violent fate that wasn't meant to be. Which is why the spirits intervened, transforming matter into pure energy. Starlight. But it's not what happened here.

Fox Mulder

How do you know that?

Harold Piller

Because these children all died suffering, pleading innocently for their lives. These beautiful children, so... Trusting and pure. I see them. My god, why? Why must some suffer and not others?

Fox Mulder

You see them? Do you see amber lynn lapierre?

Harold Piller

She wasn't here. She never was. But I'm-- I'm sensing a connection with her... To this place. No, it's a connection to-- it's a connection to you.

Fox Mulder

How's that?

Harold Piller

You lost someone close to you. A young girl. It happened a-- a long time ago. Your sister. There's a connection between these girls, isn't there? Between her and amber lynn?

Fox Mulder

What is the connection?

Harold Piller

I don't know. But we're going to find them. I'm sure of it.

Agent Schoniger

Here I became suspicious.

Samantha?

Dana Scully

Suspicious of what?

Agent Schoniger

In 30 years with the FBI, you think you've seen it all. I sometimes think I have. But this is just a garden variety compensatory abduction fantasy.

Dana Scully

Compensatory for what?

Agent Schoniger

His guilt. His fear. Everything that's preventing agent Mulder... From remembering the truth about what really happened that night.

Dana Scully

You mean his sister wasn't abducted?

Agent Schoniger

No, his sister definitely went missing in 1973. That's not in dispute. Agent Mulder, however, wasn't regressed until 1989. See, his delusion is playing into his unconscious hope... That his sister is still alive. And if you think about it, his delusion has the effect... Of giving him reason to pursue her.

Dana Scully

But why alien abduction?

Agent Schoniger

Close encounters, e.t., who knows? But there was probably a lot of imagery collecting in his head... In those 16 years. And then he comes down here, and he finds the X-Files.

Dana Scully

So what do you think happened to his sister?

Agent Schoniger

Well, in 1973... We were pretty damned unsophisticated about violent predatory crime. My guess is she was kidnapped in the house, her body was disposed of, never found.

Dana Scully

You think that his sister's dead?

Agent Schoniger

Have you seen this file? There was an extraordinary amount of effort put into finding his sister. Even the treasury department got involved. His father worked at a high level in the government. They found nothing. Why, agent Scully? Why do you wanna bring all this back up now?

Dana Scully

Someone owes it to Mulder.

Agent Schoniger

Word of advice, me to you. Let it be. You know, there are some wounds that are just too painful ever to be reopened.

Dana Scully

Well, this particular wound has never healed. And Mulder deserves closure, just like anyone.
